articles.title: Robot data startup Mecka AI nabs $60M from Sequoia
articles.full_text:
Mecka AI, a startup that collects and analyzes human motion data to train humanoid robots and other kinds of robots, announced it has raised a $60 million Series B round led by Sequoia, with participation from Nvidia, Microsoft’s venture fund M12, and others. TechCrunch had previously reported that the startup was nearing a new funding round at a $500 million valuation.

Founded in 2024, the startup intends to do for robotics what Scale AI, Mercor, Surge, and other data-labeling companies have done for LLMs. Those companies supply the human-generated data these systems learn from. Mecka pays people to record themselves doing everyday tasks, like making coffee or fixing cars, while wearing body sensors and using smartphones.

Other startups that collect real-world data for robot training include XDOF, which was in talks to raise a Series B round at a $1.2 billion valuation according to TechCrunch’s previous reporting. Human-data platforms that began with LLMs are also expanding into robotics, such as Scale AI and Micro1.
articles.summary:
Mecka AI has secured $60 million in Series B funding to expand its human motion data platform for training robots, signaling growing investor confidence in the robotics data market.

  • Funding details: The round was led by Sequoia, with participation from Nvidia, Microsoft's venture fund M12, and others. TechCrunch previously reported the startup was nearing a round at a $500 million valuation.
  • Core business: Founded in 2024, Mecka pays people to record themselves performing everyday tasks—such as making coffee or fixing cars—while wearing body sensors and using smartphones, then collects and analyzes that motion data to train humanoid and other robots.
  • Market context: Mecka aims to do for robotics what data-labeling companies like Scale AI, Mercor, and Surge have done for LLMs, supplying the human-generated data these systems learn from.
  • Competitive landscape: Other startups collecting real-world data for robot training include XDOF, which was reportedly in talks to raise a Series B at a $1.2 billion valuation, while LLM-focused data platforms like Scale AI and Micro1 are also expanding into robotics.
